name: Life of Jesus (Incarnation to Ascension)

objectives.text: Identify pictures of the manger, the cross, and the empty tomb and tell which part of Jesus' life each shows
Retell the story of Jesus' birth in Bethlehem, naming Mary, Joseph, the angels, and the shepherds
Name the twelve disciples Jesus called and retell how he called the first fishermen to follow him
Retell a miracle of Jesus, such as calming the storm or feeding the five thousand, in the correct order of events
Retell the visit of the wise men and the family's escape to Egypt
Retell the account of the boy Jesus in the temple and describe what it shows about his relationship to his Father
Retell the parables of the lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost son and explain what each teaches about God seeking sinners
State that Jesus is true God who became a true man, using John's words that the Word became flesh
Summarize the baptism and temptation of Jesus and describe the role of John the Baptist as the one who prepared his way
Locate Bethlehem, Nazareth, Capernaum, the Sea of Galilee, the Jordan River, and Jerusalem on a map and connect each to an event in Jesus' life
Explain the meaning of the incarnation as the eternal Son of God taking a true body and a reasonable soul, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary
Sequence the major events of Passion Week from the triumphal entry through the resurrection
Describe the Jewish and Roman setting of Jesus' ministry, including the synagogue, the temple, the Pharisees, the Sadducees, and Roman rule
Classify Jesus' miracles by the authority they reveal over nature, sickness, demons, and death and explain how John presents them as signs pointing to who Jesus is
Describe the resurrection appearances of Jesus and explain how they show that he rose bodily from the dead
Compare the responses of the Pharisees and of known sinners to Jesus and explain what the contrast reveals about grace and self-righteousness
Explain how specific events in Jesus' birth, ministry, and death fulfill Old Testament prophecies
Analyze the 'I Am' statements in the Gospel of John and explain how they connect to God's name revealed in Exodus
Compare how Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John each present the life of Jesus, noting their stated purposes and distinctive emphases
Explain what Jesus taught about the kingdom of God through the parables of Matthew 13
Analyze how the Sermon on the Mount describes the character and conduct of citizens of the kingdom and how Jesus relates his teaching to the Law
Connect the Transfiguration to Old Testament appearances of God's glory and explain why Moses and Elijah appear with Jesus
Explain the Reformed teaching on Christ's states of humiliation and exaltation and place the events of his life within each
Explain how the Gospels and the Reformed confessions interpret Jesus' death as a substitutionary sacrifice for sinners
Explain the significance of the Ascension, including Christ's heavenly intercession and present reign, as the Reformed confessions state it
Construct a harmony of the four Gospel accounts of Passion Week and account for differences in detail among them
Analyze how Jesus taught his disciples to read the Old Testament as testifying to his suffering and glory
Evaluate why the Reformed confessions teach that the Mediator must be true God and true man united in one person without confusion or division
Evaluate naturalistic explanations of Jesus' miracles and resurrection using the eyewitness claims of the Gospels and the apostles
Compose an essay showing how the events of Jesus' life fulfill the offices of prophet, priest, and king

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: the manger, cross, and tomb; the disciples; the lost-things parables; baptism and temptation; the incarnation; the Pharisees and sinners; the I Am statements; the Sermon on the Mount; the Transfiguration; the Ascension; the Passion harmony; the two natures; the defense of miracles; and the three offices. Replaced 'Express that Jesus is God' with an observable statement anchored to John 1. Reframed the teaching, healing, and suffering category as a classification of miracles as signs. Added the birth narrative, the wise men, the boy Jesus in the temple, individual miracles, map locations, the first-century setting, Passion Week sequencing, resurrection appearances, fulfilled prophecy, the Gospels' distinct emphases, the kingdom parables, humiliation and exaltation, the atoning death, and Jesus reading the Old Testament as testimony to himself. Pentecost and the apostolic church are left to the Early Church sibling. Anchored each objective to specific verses and to the relevant catechism and confession articles.
